findings.text: follow-on: the `domain_waiver` declaration in RECORD_FIELDS is guarded by no assertion in this node's own gate, so deleting it leaves the suite green while the field stops being part of the declared promoted shape; the repository already owns the idiom for this check (assert "key" in ledger.RECORD_FIELDS at tests/test_disposition_reaches_the_ledger_row.py:159 and tests/test_ledger_declares_the_review_tier.py:58) and the new test module did not use it.

follow-on: the parameter name `domain_waiver` carries the guard's waiver mapping inside `_complete_locked`, while the same identifier carries the reason string at reckon/crew/promotion.py:258 and reckon/mcp.py:2367, so a close reading of one waiver end to end has to check the type at each layer rather than the name; no naming rule is broken and the record is correct, so this is a comprehension cost rather than a defect.

follow-on: `waiver["reason"] == WAIVER_REASON` compares the row's reason against the constant the test itself hands the tool at line 137, so it pins carriage of the input rather than an independent reading of the row; it does redden on the regression (the field is absent, so the `waiver is not None` check at line 144 fails first), and the independent comparison is the guard-product case at line 205.
